full_judgment: 33. Learned Advocate for the petitioner of some of the Rules relied on the decisions in the case of Chiranjit Lal vs. Union of India reported in AIR 1951 SC. 41; and VG Row vs. State of Madras reported in AIR 1951 Mad. 147 in support of his contention that right of association cannot be curtailed. Madras High Court decision has no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the instant cases. In the case of Chiranjit Lal, a shareholder of Sholapur Spinning and Weaving Company Limited challenged the provisions of Sholapur Spinning and Weaving Company (Emergency Provisions) Act 1950 as it took over management of the company from the directors appointed by the share holders and deprived them from electing directors, passing resolutions and starting proceedings for winding up of the company and or for appointment of a receiver through Court. Challenges of violation of Articles 14, 19(1), and 31 of the Constitution of India similar to our Articles 27, 36-40 and 42 were negatived by the majority decision in that case. In that case following observations from the case of Middleton vs.Taxes Power and L Company reported in 249 US 152 at P 157 was quoted with approval: "It must be presumed that legislature understands, and correctly appreciates, the needs of its own people, that its laws are directed to problems made manifest by experience and that its discriminations are based upon adequate grounds."
